title: Semi-analytic Inference of Satellite Densities in the Cold Dark Matter Model Part II. Implications for Dark Matter Indirect Detection Constraints
comment: 16+9 pages, 4+6 figures, video abstract at https://youtu.be/x9zNkN6XyAA
summary: Dwarf galaxies provide excellent targets to search for signals of dark matter annihilation or decay. Using a calibrated semi-analytic model and the latest stellar kinematic data (presented in Part I), this paper updates the astrophysical J-factors for the Milky Way's dwarf spheroidal galaxies. We infer the probability distributions for the J-factors of 39 dwarfs by conditioning a population of subhalos, generated with the SatGen semi-analytic satellite model, on either a dwarf's kinematically determined dynamical mass or its stellar mass. We also compute the J-factors using the Jeans equation with updated stellar kinematics and priors that incorporate varying degrees of SatGen information. We use the computed J-factors to recast existing limits from Fermi-LAT data on the annihilation cross section. Our main result is that variations in the J-factors computed using the Jeans analysis introduce a factor of 2-4 uncertainty into the inferred limits on the cross section. We argue that a cosmologically informed prior is a motivated choice that excludes thermal relic annihilation cross sections to $b\bar{b}$ below about 70 GeV. For comparison, the more commonly used priors, which can lead to unphysical halo parameters, exclude masses below 130 GeV at 95% confidence level. We also show that the highest-J-factor dwarfs are spatially extended, approximately one degree on the sky, which challenges the validity of the point-source approximation adopted in many analyses of Fermi data. Finally, based on the semi-analytic model and the kinematic data, the highest J-factor halos have already been discovered, suggesting future ultra-faint discoveries are unlikely to substantially strengthen limits on annihilating dark matter.

AI.tldr: This paper updates the astrophysical J-factors for 39 Milky Way dwarf spheroidal galaxies using kinematic data and the SatGen semi-analytic model, combines them with Fermi-LAT data to recast dark matter annihilation limits, and finds that J-factor uncertainties introduce a factor of 2-4 uncertainty in cross-section limits. Cosmologically informed priors exclude thermal relic annihilation to bbbar below ~70 GeV, while unphysical priors exclude below 130 GeV. The highest-J dwarfs are spatially extended (~1 degree), challenging point-source approximations, and the highest-J halos have likely already been discovered.
AI.motivation: Dwarf galaxies are prime targets for detecting dark matter annihilation/decay signals, but their astrophysical J-factors carry significant uncertainties. This work aims to provide updated, cosmologically calibrated J-factors and assess how these uncertainties affect limits on the dark matter annihilation cross section inferred from Fermi-LAT data.
AI.method: The authors use the SatGen semi-analytic model to generate a population of subhalos and condition them on either the kinematically determined dynamical mass or the stellar mass of each of 39 dwarf spheroidal galaxies, thereby inferring probability distributions for the J-factors. They also compute J-factors via the Jeans equation using updated stellar kinematics with priors that incorporate varying degrees of SatGen information. The resulting J-factors are then used to recast Fermi-LAT limits on the annihilation cross section.
AI.result: Jeans analysis J-factor variations introduce a factor of 2-4 uncertainty in the inferred annihilation cross-section limits. A cosmologically informed prior excludes thermal relic annihilation to bbbar below ~70 GeV, whereas more commonly used priors (which can yield unphysical halo parameters) exclude masses below 130 GeV at 95% confidence. The highest-J-factor dwarfs are spatially extended (~1 degree on the sky), challenging the point-source approximation. The highest-J halos have already been discovered, suggesting ultra-faint future discoveries won't significantly improve limits.
AI.conclusion: The choice of priors in Jeans analysis substantially affects dark matter annihilation limits, and cosmologically motivated priors provide more physically reasonable constraints. The angular extent of high-J dwarfs warrants careful treatment beyond the point-source approximation, and the discovery space for high-J halos is largely exhausted, implying diminishing returns from future ultra-faint dwarf discoveries for annihilating dark matter searches.

title: Relativistic effects of PSR~J1856--0039 double neutron star system in a 2.36-hour compact orbit
comment: 9 pages, 4 figures, accepted by Phys. Rev. Lett
summary: Compact double neutron star (DNS) systems are unique laboratories for testing gravitational theories and studying DNS mergers. Here we report the properties of a new DNS system, PSR J1856--0039, discovered in the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST). The pulsar is mildly recycled with a period of 23.4~ms in a compact eccentric orbit ($e=0.106$) with an orbital period of 2.36 hours. By following up FAST observations, we measured the relativistic effects, including the orbital period derivative $\dot{P}_{\rm orb}=-1.284\pm0.019\times10^{-12}$ s s$^{-1}$, periastron advance $\dotω=17.5859\pm0.0007$ deg yr$^{-1}$, and Einstein delay $γ=0.445\pm0.011$ ms. This DNS system has a low orbital inclination of $i=133^\circ.2\pm1^\circ.1$ and the lowest total mass of any known DNS, $M_{\rm tot}=2.48841\pm0.00015 M\odot$, with a determined pulsar mass of $1.304\pm0.022 M_\odot$ and a companion mass of $1.185\pm0.022 M_\odot$, one of the lowest neutron-star masses. The observed orbital decay due to gravitational-wave emission $\dot{P}^{\rm GW}_{\rm orb,obs}$ and the orbital decay predicted by general relativity $\dot{P}^{\rm GW}_{\rm orb,pred}$ are consistent at a level of $\dot{P}^{\rm GW}_{\rm orb,obs}/\dot{P}^{\rm GW}_{\rm orb,pred}=$1.009(14) (68% confidence). This DNS will merge after 82 Myr and may form a stable neutron star or collapse into a black hole after spin-down. Long-term monitoring could potentially probe the Lense-Thirring precession.

AI.tldr: Discovery and characterization of PSR J1856-0039, a new compact double neutron star system found with FAST, featuring the lowest total mass of any known DNS (2.488 Msun), a low orbital inclination, and gravitational-wave orbital decay consistent with general relativity predictions.
AI.motivation: Double neutron star systems are unique laboratories for testing gravitational theories and studying DNS mergers; discovering new DNS systems with precise relativistic measurements expands the sample for such tests.
AI.method: Discovery via the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST) with follow-up observations to measure relativistic effects: orbital period derivative, periastron advance, and Einstein delay. These measurements enable determination of component masses, orbital inclination, and gravitational-wave emission rate.
AI.result: PSR J1856-0039 is a mildly recycled pulsar (P=23.4 ms) in a compact eccentric orbit (e=0.106, P_orb=2.36 hr). It has the lowest total mass of any known DNS (2.4884 Msun), a pulsar mass of 1.304 Msun, companion mass of 1.185 Msun, and low inclination (133.2 deg). The observed-to-predicted gravitational-wave orbital decay ratio is 1.009(14), consistent with GR. The system will merge in 82 Myr.
AI.conclusion: This new DNS system confirms general relativistic predictions for orbital decay, exhibits extreme low masses among DNS systems, and offers long-term monitoring opportunities to probe Lense-Thirring precession, as well as insight into post-merger outcomes (stable NS or black hole formation).

title: Exploring cosmic magnetism with gamma-ray burst afterglow emission
summary: The nature and origin of magnetic fields on cosmological scales are still unclear. Magnetic fields detected in galaxies and galaxy clusters are typically interpreted as the result of the amplification of weak seed fields, but their nature remains largely unknown with two scenarios considered: the cosmological and the astrophysical origin. Signatures of magnetization in cosmic voids from observations of very high energy (VHE, E > 100 GeV) photons from extragalactic sources can provide crucial results. Indeed, if a non-negligible intergalactic magnetic field (IGMF) is present in the voids, a time-delayed emission known as pair-echo is expected. The timing and intensity of this signal encode information on the IGMF strength B and properties. Given the recent detection of GRB afterglows at TeV energies, in this article we perform a detectability study of pair-echo signatures from GRBs. We simulate afterglow emission for different values of the jet kinetic energy (E$_{k,iso}$ = 10$^{49}$ - 10$^{55}$ erg), redshift (z = 0.03 - 1), and lightcurve break times, and estimate the expected pair-echo radiation for IGMF strengths in the range B = 10$^{-19}$ - 10$^{-16}$ G. We investigate the capability of CTAO to detect the resulting emission at tens of GeV. We find that a subsample of GRBs in the z - E$_{k,iso}$ parameter space can produce a detectable pair-echo component for CTAO for all the tested IGMF strengths. A steepening of the GRB afterglow light curve, caused e.g. by an early (0.1 - 1 days) jet break, is a key factor to increase the chances of detection. CTAO observations starting from 10 - 12 hrs up to a few days after the GRB trigger time can provide relevant results to probe IGMF.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the detectability of pair-echo signatures from gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) to probe intergalactic magnetic fields (IGMF). By simulating GRB afterglow emission across a range of jet kinetic energies, redshifts, and lightcurve break times, and estimating pair-echo radiation for IGMF strengths of B = 10^-19 to 10^-16 G, the authors find that a subsample of GRBs can produce detectable pair-echo components for the CTAO at tens of GeV. Early jet breaks (0.1-1 days) significantly increase detection chances, and CTAO observations starting 10-12 hours to a few days after the trigger can provide relevant IGMF constraints.
AI.motivation: The origin of magnetic fields on cosmological scales remains unknown, with cosmological and astrophysical scenarios competing. Magnetic-field signatures in cosmic voids, inferred from pair-echo emission in very high energy (VHE) photons from extragalactic sources, can provide crucial constraints on the intergalactic magnetic field (IGMF). The recent detection of GRB afterglows at TeV energies motivates a detectability study of pair-echo signatures from GRBs.
AI.method: The authors simulate GRB afterglow emission for different jet kinetic energies (E_k,iso = 10^49 - 10^55 erg), redshifts (z = 0.03 - 1), and lightcurve break times. They estimate the expected pair-echo radiation for IGMF strengths in the range B = 10^-19 to 10^-16 G, and assess the capability of CTAO to detect the resulting emission at tens of GeV energies.
AI.result: A subsample of GRBs in the z - E_k,iso parameter space can produce a detectable pair-echo component for CTAO across all tested IGMF strengths. A steepening of the GRB afterglow lightcurve due to an early jet break (0.1-1 days) is a key factor increasing detection chances. CTAO observations starting 10-12 hours up to a few days after the GRB trigger can yield relevant results for probing the IGMF.
AI.conclusion: GRB pair-echo emission presents a viable avenue for CTAO to probe the IGMF. Targeted observations of suitable GRBs with early jet breaks, initiated 10-12 hours to a few days post-trigger, could provide meaningful constraints on intergalactic magnetic field strengths in the range B = 10^-19 to 10^-16 G.

title: Binary neutron star populations across cosmic time: the impact of binary stellar evolution uncertainties
summary: We investigate the impact of uncertainties in binary stellar evolution on the formation efficiency and cosmological merger rate of BNS systems. In particular, we aim to determine whether robust signatures of binary evolution can be identified across a broad range of metallicities. We perform a systematic exploration of 72 binary evolution models using the population synthesis code COSMIC. We vary four key parameters controlling the onset and efficiency of common-envelope evolution, the natal kick prescription, and the treatment of kicks during the common envelope phase. For each model, we compute the BNS formation efficiency and cosmological merger rate using several prescriptions for the cosmic metallicity-redshift relation. We identify characteristic features in the metallicity dependence of the BNS formation efficiency that arise from specific evolutionary processes. These include the onset of first-giant-branch skipping at low metallicity and a non-monotonic evolution between $Z=10^{-3}$ and $7.5\times 10^{-3}$. All models also predict a bimodal distribution of BNS progenitor masses associated with two distinct formation channels. The common envelope ejection efficiency and natal kick prescription remain the dominant sources of uncertainty, producing variations of several orders of magnitude in both the BNS formation efficiency and the cosmological merger rate. Finally, we show that different combinations of binary-evolution parameters can produce similar merger-rate histories, highlighting significant degeneracies among population-synthesis models. Current gravitational-wave observations can rule out only the least efficient formation scenarios. Breaking these degeneracies will require larger samples of BNS mergers expected from future third-generation gravitational-wave observatories, and improved observational constraints on the evolution of metallicity across cosmic time.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically explores 72 binary stellar evolution models using COSMIC population synthesis to investigate how common-envelope evolution, natal kicks, and kick treatment during CE affect BNS formation efficiency and cosmological merger rates across metallicities. Key findings include characteristic metallicity-dependent features (such as first-giant-branch skipping and non-monotonic evolution), a bimodal progenitor mass distribution, and that CE ejection efficiency and natal kick prescription dominate uncertainties, producing orders-of-magnitude variations. Significant model degeneracies exist, and current gravitational-wave observations can only rule out the least efficient formation scenarios.
AI.motivation: To determine whether robust signatures of binary stellar evolution can be identified across a broad range of metallicities for BNS systems, and to assess the impact of key binary-evolution uncertainties on formation efficiency and merger rates.
AI.method: Systematic exploration of 72 binary evolution models using the population synthesis code COSMIC, varying four parameters: onset and efficiency of common-envelope evolution, natal kick prescription, and treatment of kicks during the CE phase. BNS formation efficiency and cosmological merger rates were computed using multiple prescriptions for the cosmic metallicity-redshift relation.
AI.result: Identified characteristic metallicity-dependent features in BNS formation efficiency, including first-giant-branch skipping at low metallicity and non-monotonic evolution between Z=10^-3 and 7.5×10^-3. All models predict a bimodal progenitor mass distribution from two formation channels. CE ejection efficiency and natal kick prescription dominate uncertainties, causing variations of several orders of magnitude. Current gravitational-wave observations can only exclude the least efficient scenarios due to significant parameter degeneracies.
AI.conclusion: Breaking model degeneracies will require larger BNS merger samples from future third-generation gravitational-wave observatories and improved observational constraints on the cosmic metallicity evolution.

title: Semi-analytic Inference of Satellite Densities in the Cold Dark Matter Model Part I. Comparison to Ultra-faint Dwarf Kinematics
comment: 22+11 pages, 8+6 figures, video abstract at https://youtu.be/dal8_lRz3EI
summary: Ultra-faint dwarf galaxies are critical testing grounds for probing the limits of galaxy formation in the cold dark matter (CDM) paradigm. Employing a semi-analytic cosmological satellite generator that captures the expected CDM halo population, we estimate Milky Way dwarf density profiles through two methods: a kinematic approach using stellar velocity dispersions and a separate method based on dwarf stellar masses. The kinematic approach yields a larger diversity in central dark matter densities than expected from the CDM population, as inferred from the stellar-to-halo mass relation, with compact ultra-faints appearing overdense and larger systems appearing underdense. For the ultra-faint dwarfs with at least 10 stars with spectroscopic measurements, this discrepancy persists at the ~2.4$σ$ level across all considered systematic variations on the semi-analytic modeling. Our framework introduces a novel, robust procedure for testing the consistency of the observed population of Milky Way satellites with cosmological expectations. As future surveys discover new dwarf satellites and refine stellar velocity measurements, updating this analysis will provide an increasingly stringent test of the CDM paradigm.

AI.tldr: This paper tests the cold dark matter (CDM) paradigm using ultra-faint dwarf galaxies around the Milky Way. Using a semi-analytic cosmological satellite generator, the authors estimate dwarf density profiles via two methods (kinematic and stellar-mass-based). They find that the kinematic approach produces greater diversity in central dark matter densities than expected from CDM, with compact ultra-faints appearing overdense and larger systems underdense. This discrepancy persists at ~2.4σ for ultra-faint dwarfs with ≥10 spectroscopically measured stars, suggesting a potential tension with CDM predictions that will be refined as more data becomes available.
AI.motivation: Ultra-faint dwarf galaxies are the most extreme low-mass systems known and serve as critical tests of whether the CDM paradigm can accurately predict galaxy formation at the smallest scales. Testing whether observed Milky Way satellite populations are consistent with CDM expectations is key to validating or challenging the standard cosmological model.
AI.method: The authors employ a semi-analytic cosmological satellite generator that captures the expected CDM halo population around the Milky Way. They estimate dwarf galaxy density profiles using two independent approaches: (1) a kinematic method based on stellar velocity dispersions, and (2) a method based on dwarf stellar masses and the stellar-to-halo mass relation.
AI.result: The kinematic approach reveals a larger diversity in central dark matter densities than predicted by the CDM halo population derived from the stellar-to-halo mass relation. Compact ultra-faint dwarfs appear overdense while larger systems appear underdense relative to expectations. For ultra-faint dwarfs with at least 10 stars with spectroscopic data, this discrepancy holds at the ~2.4σ level across all considered systematic variations in the semi-analytic modeling.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a novel, robust procedure for testing the consistency of observed Milky Way satellite populations with cosmological expectations. The ~2.4σ discrepancy indicates a potential tension with CDM predictions at the smallest galaxy scales. Future surveys discovering more dwarf satellites and improving stellar velocity measurements will make this test increasingly stringent, offering a pathway to either confirm or resolve this apparent inconsistency with the CDM paradigm.

title: Radio Follow-Up of Einstein Probe Fast X-Ray Transients
summary: Fast X-ray transients (FXTs) are brief, luminous bursts of soft X-ray emission whose physical origins remain uncertain. The Einstein Probe (EP) mission has recently enabled prompt discovery of these events, providing opportunities for rapid multi-wavelength follow-up. We present a coordinated radio observing campaign targeting 20 FXTs detected by the EP in 2024. The core consists of 59 epochs with the Allen Telescope Array (ATA), sampling post-burst timescales from $\sim$1 to $\sim$65 days and reaching typical $3σ$ sensitivities of 0.6--1.5\,mJy across 1--8\,GHz. Two FXTs---EP240315a and EP241021a---have radio counterparts. For EP241021a, AMI-LA monitoring at 15.5\,GHz reveals a light curve peaking at $\sim$30 days with $F_ν\approx1.0$\,mJy; equipartition analysis implies a Newtonian equipartition energy of $\sim3\times10^{49}$\,erg and a mildly relativistic on-axis solution with $Γ_{\rm on}\approx1.3$. Multi-frequency modelling of EP240315a, combining new VLA measurements with published MeerKAT, ATCA, and eMERLIN data, indicates highly relativistic early emission ($Γ\gtrsim3$) that decelerates with time, consistent with jetted outflow. The detections and ATA non-detections span luminosities overlapping the brightest GRB and relativistic tidal disruption event (TDE) afterglows, suggesting FXTs comprise a heterogeneous population including both relativistic and non-relativistic explosions. Under a GRB-like redshift prior, our $3σ$ ATA limits correspond to observer-frame specific-luminosity thresholds of $\sim10^{32}$--$10^{33}\,\mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}\ Hz^{-1}}$; for nearby events ($z\lesssim0.2$), $L_ν\lesssim10^{30\text{--}31}\,\mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}\ Hz^{-1}}$. Planned ATA upgrades and next-generation arrays (SKA, DSA, ngVLA) will enable sensitive, population-level radio studies of the FXT radio sky.

The Einstein Probe mission now enables prompt discovery and rapid multi-wavelength follow-up, motivating a systematic radio campaign to characterize these events and discriminate between possible progenitor scenarios (e.g., relativistic jets vs. non-relativistic explosions).

title: Superdiffusion at the Galactic Centre
summary: Tracking S-star cluster orbits around Sgr A* calibrates orbital transport models for space-borne gravitational wave detectors. Standard kinetic theories model this cluster via local Fokker-Planck equations, which predict that general relativistic precession halts angular momentum diffusion at the Schwarzschild barrier. Because inverse-square gravitational encounters generate a Holtsmark torque distribution with infinite variance, resonant relaxation operates as a space-fractional process governed by non-local Lévy flights. We simulate this superdiffusive continuous-time random walk using a Markov chain initialized with empirical S-star orbits, including the recently observd S301. Integro-differential fractional operators allow trajectories to cross regions of quenched local diffusion without density buildup at the barrier. Non-equilibrium regimes yield immediate linear flux growth, while secular tidal heating at periastron inflates stellar radii to shift disruption boundaries. Regularized backward integration of the fractional transport equation traces current phase space configurations back to initial deposition states, matching the energy requirements of the \emph{Fermi} bubbles. Relativistic precession does not suppress mass-ratio inspiral rates, which provides a model for event topologies in target galactic nuclei.

AI.tldr: The paper models the S-star cluster orbiting Sgr A* using space-fractional Fokker-Planck kinetic theory, showing that resonant relaxation operates as a superdiffusive Lévy flight process. Simulations with a Markov chain initialized from empirical orbits (including newly observed S301) reveal that fractional operators allow trajectories to cross the Schwarzschild barrier without density buildup, and that relativistic precession does not suppress mass-ratio inspiral rates—offering a model for Fermi bubble energy requirements and inspiral event topologies in galactic nuclei.
AI.motivation: Standard local Fokker-Planck kinetic theory predicts that general relativistic precession halts angular momentum diffusion at the Schwarzschild barrier. However, inverse-square gravitational encounters produce a Holtsmark torque distribution with infinite variance, meaning resonant relaxation is fundamentally non-local and superdiffusive—requiring a fractional kinetic framework to correctly model S-star cluster dynamics and calibrate orbital transport for space-borne gravitational wave detectors.
AI.method: The study simulates a superdiffusive continuous-time random walk as a Markov chain initialized with empirical S-star orbits (including the newly observed S301). The transport is governed by integro-differential fractional operators that permit trajectories to cross regions of quenched local diffusion. Additionally, regularized backward integration of the fractional transport equation is used to trace present phase-space configurations back to initial deposition states.
AI.result: Non-equilibrium regimes yield immediate linear flux growth; secular tidal heating at periastron inflates stellar radii, shifting disruption boundaries. Backward integration matches the energy requirements of Fermi bubbles. Contrary to standard predictions, relativistic precession does not suppress mass-ratio inspiral rates, providing a model for event topologies in target galactic nuclei.
AI.conclusion: The S-star cluster around Sgr A* must be described by space-fractional transport rather than local Fokker-Planck equations. Fractional kinetic theory captures barrier-crossing trajectories, reproduces Fermi bubble energetics, and indicates that relativistic precession does not inhibit mass-ratio inspirals, with implications for gravitational wave detector calibration and galactic nucleus event modeling.

title: On the triple nature of the PSR J0435+3233 system
summary: Context. The recent pulsar timing ephemeris of PSR J0435+3233 indicates that this millisecond pulsar (MSP) has a spin-down rate that is much higher than observed in other MSPs and challenges our understanding of the formation and evolution of MSPs. Aims. We propose that this system is a hierarchical triple, and that the high spin-down rate is caused by varying acceleration due to a tertiary in a wide orbit. Methods. We use pulsar timing methods with radio and gamma-ray observations of PSR J0435+3233 to determine the system properties. Results. We find that a hierarchical triple timing model describes the timing observations of PSR J0435+3233 and that this results in the detection of gamma-ray pulsations back to the beginning of the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) data in 2008. The intrinsic spin-down rate remains uncertain as it correlates with the parameters of the outer orbit, but large spin-down rates are excluded and the intrinsic rate is at least two orders of magnitude lower than the observed rate, in line with other Galactic MSPs. We identify a star located 11 mas from the pulsar position as the optical counterpart to the tertiary companion. From the 1.5-2.5 kpc distance and colours, we infer that the tertiary is a 1.2 solar mass F-type main-sequence star. Along with the pulsar binary, it orbits the common centre of mass with an eccentric (e ~ 0.6), wide (~ 70 yr) orbit that is likely seen at a low orbital inclination. Conclusions. We conclude that PSR J0435+3233 is a hierarchical triple system. We discuss the motivation and prospects for the continued study of this system. Spectral measurements of the outer star in addition to continued astrometric measurements will yield mass ratio and inclination estimates, while continued pulsar timing may yield a tighter constraint on violations of the Strong Equivalence Principle than are currently obtained from PSR J0337+1715.

AI.tldr: PSR J0435+3233, a millisecond pulsar with an anomalously high observed spin-down rate, is shown to be a hierarchical triple system. The apparent high spin-down is caused by acceleration from a wide-orbit tertiary (a 1.2 solar mass, F-type main-sequence star in a ~70 yr, eccentric orbit), and the intrinsic spin-down rate is at least two orders of magnitude lower, consistent with other Galactic MSPs.
AI.motivation: The pulsar's observed spin-down rate is much higher than in other MSPs, challenging our understanding of MSP formation and evolution. The authors propose that this anomaly is not physical but rather arises from a hierarchical triple configuration with a tertiary in a wide orbit.
AI.method: Pulsar timing methods are applied to radio and gamma-ray (Fermi-LAT) observations of PSR J0435+3233. A hierarchical triple timing model is fit to the data, enabling the detection of gamma-ray pulsations back to 2008. The optical counterpart of the tertiary is identified astrometrically, and its properties are inferred from distance and photometric colors.
AI.result: The hierarchical triple model describes the timing observations well and yields gamma-ray pulsations since 2008. Large intrinsic spin-down rates are excluded; the intrinsic rate is at least two orders of magnitude below the observed rate, in line with other MSPs. An 11 mas-separated optical star is the counterpart to a 1.2 solar-mass F-type main-sequence tertiary in an eccentric (e~0.6), wide (~70 yr) orbit likely seen at low inclination, at 1.5-2.5 kpc.
AI.conclusion: PSR J0435+3233 is a hierarchical triple system. Continued study—spectral measurements of the outer star, astrometry, and continued pulsar timing—will yield mass ratio and inclination constraints and may improve Strong Equivalence Principle violation limits beyond those from PSR J0337+1715.

title: The influence of feedback on the baryonic content of haloes in the COLIBRE simulations
comment: 25 pages, 11 figures. Submitted to MNRAS, comments welcome
summary: We present predictions for the relation between the halo gas mass fraction and halo mass, $f_{\rm gas}^{200}-M_{200}$, from the COLIBRE cosmological simulations of galaxy formation, and explore how the gas content of haloes is influenced by feedback from supernovae and active galactic nuclei (AGN) over time. The $f_{\rm gas}^{200}-M_{200}$ relation in COLIBRE is non-monotonic, with a peak at $M_{200}\sim 10^{11.5-12}$~M$_\odot$. Below this mass, feedback from supernovae efficiently expels gas from the haloes of dwarf galaxies, and above it, AGN feedback efficiently depletes the haloes of galaxy groups. The fiducial COLIBRE model yields gas fractions for galaxy groups and clusters that agree with constraints from Chandra and XMM-Newton X-ray data, but which are high relative to gas fractions inferred from eROSITA stacks and measurements of the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel-dovich (kSZ) effect. COLIBRE's hybrid AGN feedback model, which combines thermal and jet-driven feedback, produces lower gas fractions in better agreement with eROSITA and kSZ measurements. COLIBRE produces lower gas fractions for groups and clusters than EAGLE and other contemporary simulations, and better agreement with observational constraints. We investigate the origin of this improvement relative to EAGLE, and how the resolution of the simulation affects the impact of feedback. Our results demonstrate that halo gas fractions are a sensitive probe of feedback physics, and that they can differ significantly between simulations that otherwise produce very similar galaxy populations.

AI.tldr: The paper presents predictions for the halo gas mass fraction-halo mass relation (f_gas^200-M_200) from the COLIBRE cosmological simulations, showing a non-monotonic relation peaked at M_200~10^11.5-12 M_sun, shaped by supernova feedback in dwarf haloes and AGN feedback in group/cluster haloes. COLIBRE's hybrid AGN feedback (thermal + jet) yields lower gas fractions in better agreement with eROSITA and kSZ observations, outperforming EAGLE and contemporary simulations, demonstrating that halo gas fractions are a sensitive probe of feedback physics.
AI.motivation: To understand how feedback from supernovae and AGN shapes the gas content of dark matter haloes across mass scales, and to evaluate whether current galaxy formation simulations produce halo gas fractions consistent with X-ray, eROSITA, and kSZ observations.
AI.method: Analysis of the COLIBRE cosmological simulations of galaxy formation, comparing the f_gas^200-M_200 relation to EAGLE and other contemporary simulations, and benchmarking against observational constraints from Chandra, XMM-Newton, eROSITA, and kSZ measurements. The study examines the role of COLIBRE's hybrid AGN feedback model (thermal + jet-driven) and investigates resolution effects on feedback impact.
AI.result: The f_gas^200-M_200 relation in COLIBRE is non-monotonic with a peak at M_200~10^11.5-12 M_sun. Supernova feedback expels gas below this mass, while AGN feedback depletes gas above it. The fiducial model agrees with Chandra/XMM-Newton but overpredicts gas fractions relative to eROSITA and kSZ. The hybrid AGN feedback model produces lower gas fractions in better agreement with these observations. COLIBRE yields lower gas fractions for groups/clusters than EAGLE and other simulations, with improved observational agreement. The study identifies the origin of improvement over EAGLE and the role of resolution.
AI.conclusion: Halo gas fractions are a highly sensitive diagnostic of feedback physics, and simulations that produce very similar galaxy populations can differ significantly in their predicted halo gas content. COLIBRE's hybrid AGN feedback model offers improved agreement with a broad range of observational constraints.

title: JWST Spectra Indicate a Large Mass of Postshock Dust Formed by SN 2010jl
summary: We present new JWST mid-IR spectra and ground-based optical spectra of the lingering source at the position of SN 2010jl, which was a relatively nearby superluminous Type IIn supernova having strong interaction with circumstellar material (CSM). Early-time data showed evidence of dust, interpreted as either pre-existing CSM dust, or as newly formed dust in the SN ejecta and post-shock region. At 13 yr post explosion, JWST reveals a strong MIR excess from warm dust, with broad features at 10-15 $μ$m. Our analysis reveals a minimum dust mass of $>$0.11 $M_{\odot}$, and a more likely value of 0.2 $M_{\odot}$ or more because the dust is optically thick. This is among the largest masses of SN-produced dust yet measured without far-IR/submm data, and greatly exceeds SN 2010jl's dust mass inferred around 2-3 yr post-explosion. Ground-based optical spectra confirm the presence of a young massive cluster at the SN position, and confirm that blueshifted line profiles persisting until the latest epochs arise from dust formed in the post-shock region. The warmest dust emitting in the MIR is likely to be the same post-shock dust causing the blueshift. The JWST spectrum also reveals silicate absorption, which may arise from cool SN ejecta dust along the line of sight to the receding shock. The large mass of post-shock dust in SN 2010jl suggests that strong CSM interaction promotes efficient dust production, where the new post-shock dust will survive. If strongly interacting SNe are common in the early Universe, this may contribute significantly to dust seen in infant galaxies.

AI.tldr: New JWST mid-IR and ground-based optical spectra of the lingering source at SN 2010jl's position at 13 years post-explosion reveal a large mass of warm dust (>0.11 M☉, likely 0.2 M☉ or more due to optical thickness), making it among the largest SN-produced dust masses measured without far-IR/submm data. The dust is formed in the post-shock region (confirmed by blueshifted line profiles), and the finding suggests strong CSM interaction promotes efficient dust production that may contribute significantly to dust in early-Universe galaxies.
AI.motivation: SN 2010jl is a nearby superluminous Type IIn supernova with strong CSM interaction. Early-time observations showed dust but could not conclusively determine whether it was pre-existing CSM dust or newly formed dust in the SN ejecta/post-shock region. This paper aims to resolve this ambiguity and quantify the dust mass at 13 years post-explosion using JWST's unique mid-IR capabilities.
AI.method: The authors obtained JWST mid-infrared spectra of the lingering source at the SN 2010jl position, combined with ground-based optical spectra. They analyzed the MIR excess from warm dust, examined broad spectral features at 10-15 μm, measured silicate absorption, and computed dust mass lower limits by considering the dust's optical thickness. Optical spectra confirmed the presence of a young massive cluster and blueshifted line profiles from post-shock dust.
AI.result: JWST reveals a strong MIR excess from warm dust with broad features at 10-15 μm. Minimum dust mass is >0.11 M☉, with a more likely value of 0.2 M☉ or more due to the dust being optically thick. This is among the largest SN-produced dust masses yet measured without far-IR/submm data, greatly exceeding the dust mass inferred around 2-3 years post-explosion. Silicate absorption is also detected, possibly from cool SN ejecta dust along the line of sight to the receding shock.
AI.conclusion: The large mass of post-shock dust in SN 2010jl indicates that strong CSM interaction promotes efficient dust production, and the newly formed post-shock dust will survive. If strongly interacting SNe are common in the early Universe, they may contribute significantly to the dust observed in infant galaxies.

title: An Exploratory Analysis of New Large Gaia-informed Quasar Samples in SDSS-V
comment: Resubmitted to ApJ on 28 July 2026 after addressing the referee report. The data will be available in SDSS-V/DR20
summary: Quasars are luminous objects that provide insights into the physics and evolution of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) and their accretion flows, galaxy evolution, and even cosmology. In this study, we present an exploratory study based on the ongoing fifth generation of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS-V) and its unique dual-hemisphere, wide-field, and multi-object spectroscopic capabilities, with the aim of creating a comprehensive, all-sky quasar sample. The targets were selected through two novel methods, GUA and Skewt-QSO, that rely primarily on data from WISE and Gaia, aiming to address gaps in previous large quasar samples. Our sample includes over 250,000 spectroscopically confirmed quasars reaching z~5, with tens of thousands of newly identified quasars in the southern hemisphere. The selection methods are highly pure, with well over 80% of the spectra collected being genuine quasars; the main contaminants are M-type stars. The detailed spectral decomposition procedure we employed shows that the quasars in the sample span a wide range of luminosities (Lbol~$10^{44}-10^{48} erg s^{-1}$), SMBH masses (MBH~$10^6-10^{10}$ Msun), and accretion rates (L/LEdd~0.01-1). The distributions of these properties are consistent with those of previous quasar catalogs, which are based on past generations of SDSS, once we account for potential selection biases related to the various survey depths. Our findings confirm that novel selection methods based on optical+IR colors and/or astrometry can yield a large, high-purity quasar sample over wide sky areas, including in cases where more nuanced multi-band photometry and/or multi-wavelength data in the X-ray or radio is not available. This SDSS-V sample, which will continue to grow, establishes a robust reference for future southern (time-domain) surveys, while enhancing and complementing our understanding of quasar demographics and SMBH evolution.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an exploratory study using SDSS-V's dual-hemisphere spectroscopic capabilities to construct a comprehensive all-sky quasar sample. Using two novel selection methods (GUA and Skewt-QSO) based on WISE and Gaia data, the authors compiled over 250,000 spectroscopically confirmed quasars up to z~5, including tens of thousands of new southern-hemisphere quasars. The sample achieves high purity (>80%, main contaminants are M-type stars) and spans broad ranges of luminosity (Lbol~10^44-10^48 erg s^-1), black hole mass (MBH~10^6-10^10 Msun), and accretion rates (L/LEdd~0.01-1), consistent with previous SDSS-based catalogs after accounting for selection biases. The study demonstrates that optical+IR color and/or astrometry-based selections can yield large, high-purity quasar samples across wide sky areas even without multi-wavelength X-ray or radio data.
AI.motivation: To address gaps in previous large quasar samples (particularly in the southern hemisphere) and to exploit SDSS-V's unique dual-hemisphere, wide-field, multi-object spectroscopic capabilities to build a comprehensive all-sky quasar sample using novel selection methods.
AI.method: Using SDSS-V spectroscopy combined with two novel target selection methods, GUA and Skewt-QSO, which rely primarily on WISE infrared and Gaia optical/astrometric data. Targets were selected via optical+IR colors and/or astrometry, followed by spectral decomposition to characterize the quasar physical properties.
AI.result: Compiled a sample of over 250,000 spectroscopically confirmed quasars reaching z~5, with tens of thousands newly identified in the southern hemisphere. Selection purity exceeds 80% (with M-type stars as main contaminants). The quasars span luminosities of 10^44-10^48 erg s^-1, black hole masses of 10^6-10^10 Msun, and Eddington ratios of 0.01-1. Property distributions are consistent with previous SDSS catalogs after accounting for selection biases.
AI.conclusion: Novel selection methods based on optical+IR colors and/or astrometry can effectively produce large, high-purity quasar samples over wide sky areas, even without multi-wavelength X-ray or radio data. The SDSS-V sample provides a robust reference for future southern time-domain surveys and enhances our understanding of quasar demographics and SMBH evolution.

title: Depolarization Induced by Rapid Polarization Angle Swings: A Common Feature of Pulsars and Fast Radio Bursts?
summary: The polarization angle (PA) of pulsars and fast radio bursts (FRBs) provides a useful diagnostic of the magnetic fields in their emission regions and is therefore crucial for understanding their radiation and origins. Within a general geometric framework for polarized emission from a rotating neutron star, we suggest a possible anti-correlation between the degree of linear polarization $Π_\text{L}$ and $d\text{PA}/dt$, the time derivative of the PA, as a common feature of pulsars and FRBs. The depolarization arises from the incoherent superposition of radiation with different polarization directions within the observable part of the emission region, and is detectable only when the PA swing is steep enough. We test this conjecture using a sample of radio pulsars and find possible evidence for the expected anti-correlation in a subset of pulsars. Whether this relation holds in FRBs remains uncertain due to limited observational data. Identification of this feature would not only provide insights into the rotating magnetospheric origin of FRBs, but also place constraints on the spin periods and geometric parameters of the neutron stars that power these mysterious bursts.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes that pulsars and fast radio bursts (FRBs) may exhibit a common anti-correlation between the degree of linear polarization (Π_L) and the time derivative of the polarization angle (dPA/dt), arising from incoherent superposition of radiation with different polarization directions within the emission region. Observational evidence from a subset of radio pulsars supports this conjecture, though FRB confirmation remains uncertain.
AI.motivation: The polarization angle of pulsars and FRBs is a key diagnostic for probing magnetic fields in their emission regions and understanding their emission mechanisms and origins. Establishing a common polarization signature across both phenomena could reveal shared magnetospheric physics.
AI.method: The authors develop a general geometric framework for polarized emission from a rotating neutron star, in which depolarization results from incoherent superposition of radiation with different polarization directions within the observable emission region. They test the predicted anti-correlation between Π_L and dPA/dt using a sample of radio pulsars.
AI.result: Possible evidence for the expected anti-correlation is found in a subset of radio pulsars. The relationship remains uncertain in FRBs due to limited observational data.
AI.conclusion: If confirmed, this feature would provide insights into the rotating magnetospheric origin of FRBs and constrain the spin periods and geometric parameters of the neutron stars powering them.

title: Exploring the Limits of Spectral Line Stacking in Spectral Line Data and Application Toward the Detection of Bulk $^{13}$C Enrichment of Aromatics in TMC-1
summary: The formation history of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in the interstellar medium remains a topic of active debate, with proposed mechanisms ranging from high-temperature stellar ejecta processes to low-temperature chemistry within molecular clouds. Recently, the identification of small PAHs in the cold, dark cloud TMC-1 has provided some circumstantial evidence of the latter. If these are formed in situ, their isotopic ratios, particularly $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C, should reflect the local, bulk material of the molecular cloud; in contrast, PAHs formed in the circumstellar envelopes of evolved stars may show enhanced $^{13}$C abundances. The expected radio signals of these $^{13}$C substituted species will be faint, and thus we conducted a detailed proof-of-concept analysis examining whether spectral line stacking and matched filtering techniques can robustly retrieve signal from multiple singly substituted $^{13}$C isotopologues in aggregate. We find that while retrieved signal decreases in the limit of spectral line confusion, false-positive detections are exceedingly improbable at the adopted 5$σ$ matched filter response detection threshold. We then demonstrate the technique on actual observational data of isotopologues of HC$_9$N toward TMC-1. Finally, we show using synthetic data that if laboratory rotational spectra of all singly substituted $^{13}$C isotopologues of cyanonaphthalene and cyanopyrene isomers existed, current observations of TMC-1 would be sensitive enough to discriminate between a local, bulk $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio and one with an enhanced $^{13}$C abundance suggestive of inheritance.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the formation history of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in the interstellar medium by analyzing 13C isotope ratios. The authors conduct a proof-of-concept study using spectral line stacking and matched filtering to retrieve weak signals from singly substituted 13C isotopologues, demonstrate the technique on HC9N observations toward TMC-1, and show via synthetic data that current observations could discriminate between local in-situ PAH formation and circumstellar inheritance based on 12C/13C ratios.
AI.motivation: The formation mechanism of PAHs in the interstellar medium is debated—whether they form in high-temperature stellar ejecta or via low-temperature chemistry in molecular clouds. Small PAHs recently detected in the cold dark cloud TMC-1 provide potential evidence for in-situ formation. The authors aim to determine if PAH 12C/13C isotopic ratios can discriminate between these formation pathways, since in-situ formation should reflect local cloud material while circumstellar formation may show enhanced 13C.
AI.method: The authors perform a proof-of-concept analysis using spectral line stacking and matched filtering techniques to retrieve weak signals from multiple singly substituted 13C isotopologues in aggregate. They assess detection thresholds, signal retrieval under spectral line confusion, and false-positive rates at a 5σ matched filter detection threshold. The technique is then demonstrated on actual observational data of HC9N isotopologues toward TMC-1, followed by synthetic data simulations for cyanonaphthalene and cyanopyrene isotopologues.
AI.result: The analysis shows that while retrieved signal decreases under spectral line confusion, false-positive detections are exceedingly improbable at the adopted 5σ matched filter detection threshold. The technique is successfully demonstrated on real HC9N isotopologue observations toward TMC-1. Synthetic data simulations indicate that if laboratory rotational spectra existed for all singly substituted 13C isotopologues of cyanonaphthalene and cyanopyrene, current TMC-1 observations would be sensitive enough to distinguish local bulk 12C/13C ratios from enhanced 13C abundances suggestive of inheritance.
AI.conclusion: The matched filtering/line stacking approach is a viable and robust technique for retrieving faint 13C isotopologue signals from PAH species in cold molecular clouds. The method could provide a powerful observational test to discriminate between in-situ low-temperature PAH formation and circumstellar inheritance mechanisms, provided laboratory spectra for all relevant isotopologues become available.

title: An extra hard spectral component peaking at sub-GeV in the prompt emission of GRB 260226A
summary: The prompt emission spectra of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) have long been empirically described by the Band function over the keV--MeV range, whereas several \textit{Fermi}/LAT-detected GRBs show evidence for an extra hard component at higher energies. Here we present a joint GBM--LAT study of GRB~260226A, a rare LAT seeded onboard trigger GRB, and find that an extra sub-GeV component is present. In the time-resolved analysis, we find that a cutoff power-law model fits the spectral data of the extra component better than other models at earlier times, while at later times, the broken power-law model is preferred (or at least equally good). Interpreting the early cutoff as the $γγ$ absorption implies that the Lorentz factor at early time is lower and increases with time. The low ratio between the peak energy of the extra component and that of the Band component is difficult to explain with a one-zone synchrotron self-Compton (SSC) scenario. Two-zone emission models, such as external inverse Compton scattering of the photosphere emission by relativistic electrons accelerated in internal shocks, could provide a possible explanation.

AI.tldr: A joint GBM-LAT spectral analysis of GRB 260226A reveals an extra sub-GeV component beyond the standard Band function. The component evolves from a cutoff power-law at early times to a broken power-law at later times, suggesting a time-increasing Lorentz factor. The spectral properties are difficult to reconcile with one-zone SSC models and favor two-zone emission scenarios such as external inverse Compton scattering of photosphere emission by electrons accelerated in internal shocks.
AI.motivation: While the Band function well describes GRB prompt spectra in the keV-MeV range, some Fermi/LAT-detected GRBs show an additional hard component at higher energies that the Band function cannot account for. Understanding the origin and spectral evolution of this extra component is crucial for constraining GRB emission mechanisms and jet physics.
AI.method: The authors perform a joint GBM-LAT time-resolved spectral analysis of GRB 260226A, a rare LAT onboard-triggered GRB. They compare different spectral models (cutoff power-law, broken power-law, etc.) for the extra sub-GeV component. They interpret the early cutoff as due to gamma-gamma (γγ) absorption to derive the Lorentz factor, and test the spectral ratios against one-zone synchrotron self-Compton (SSC) and two-zone emission models.
AI.result: An extra sub-GeV component is detected in GRB 260226A. At early times a cutoff power-law best fits the extra component, while at later times a broken power-law is preferred. The inferred Lorentz factor is lower at early times and increases with time. The low peak-energy ratio between the extra and Band components disfavors a one-zone SSC interpretation, but two-zone models (external inverse Compton scattering of photosphere emission) remain viable.
AI.conclusion: The extra sub-GeV component in GRB 260226A exhibits temporal spectral evolution consistent with a time-increasing Lorentz factor, and its spectral properties point toward two-zone emission geometries rather than a simple one-zone SSC scenario. This highlights the need for multi-zone models to account for the high-energy emission in GRBs.

title: Cosmic Pairs: A DESI Census of Dual and Offset AGN as Precursors to Massive Black Hole Binaries
comment: 38 pages, 18 figures, 1 table. To be submitted to ApJ
summary: We present a systematic census of dual and offset active galactic nuclei (AGN) using spectroscopic data from the first data release (DR1) of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). After correcting for observational systematics, our final sample contains $>7,000$ dual AGN and 27,000 galaxy pairs containing one AGN over the redshift range $0 \lesssim z \lesssim 3.6$. This sample expands the known dual AGN sample by $\sim 1-2$ orders of magnitude at $0.2 \lesssim z \lesssim 0.4$, includes $\sim 50$ dwarf dual AGN candidates in a regime where only a handful were previously known, and triples the census at $z>2$. Dual AGN are preferentially found at small separations, consistent with merger-driven triggering of AGN activity. The two members of a pair differ in their star formation response: the more massive (primary) host changes little with separation, while the less massive (secondary) lies $\sim 0.3$ dex above matched inactive and one-AGN companions at the same projected separation in main-sequence offset. Using ASTRID simulations, we predict that the fraction of DESI dual AGN whose central black holes will merge by $z \sim 0$ increases with redshift, reaching $\sim 76\%$ by $z \sim 2$, while the fraction producing LISA-detectable mergers peaks at $\sim 37\%$ near $z \sim 0.9$. These results provide the largest uniformly selected spectroscopic sample of kpc-scale dual and offset AGN candidates from a single survey, connecting their host-galaxy and AGN demographics to the progenitor population of massive black hole mergers detectable by LISA.

AI.tldr: Using DESI DR1 spectroscopic data, the authors construct the largest uniformly selected sample of dual and offset AGN (>7,000 dual AGN and 27,000 one-AGN pairs) spanning 0 ≲ z ≲ 3.6, expanding known samples by 1-2 orders of magnitude at intermediate redshifts. They find dual AGN preferentially at small separations, differences in star formation response between primary and secondary hosts, and use ASTRID simulations to predict that up to ~76% of pairs will merge their black holes by z~0 and ~37% produce LISA-detectable mergers.
AI.motivation: Large uniformly selected samples of dual and offset AGN are essential for understanding merger-driven AGN triggering and connecting observed AGN pairs to the progenitor population of massive black hole mergers detectable by gravitational-wave observatories like LISA. Previous samples were small, fragmented, or limited to narrow redshift ranges.
AI.method: The authors use spectroscopic data from DESI DR1 to systematically identify dual and offset AGN, correcting for observational systematics. They analyze host-galaxy properties (including star formation offsets relative to main sequence) as a function of projected separation and pair composition, and use the ASTRID cosmological simulation to predict merger fractions and LISA-detectable merger rates for the DESI sample.
AI.result: The final sample contains >7,000 dual AGN and 27,000 one-AGN pairs over 0 ≲ z ≲ 3.6—an expansion by 1-2 orders of magnitude at 0.2 ≲ z ≲ 0.4, ~50 dwarf dual AGN candidates, and tripling of the census at z>2. Dual AGN are preferentially found at small separations. The secondary host lies ~0.3 dex above matched controls in main-sequence offset while the primary is unchanged. Simulations predict ~76% black hole merger fraction by z~0 for z~2 pairs and ~37% LISA-detectable merger fraction peaking near z~0.9.
AI.conclusion: This work provides the largest uniformly selected spectroscopic sample of kpc-scale dual and offset AGN from a single survey, connecting host-galaxy and AGN demographics to the progenitor population of massive black hole mergers detectable by LISA, with implications for merger-driven AGN triggering and the gravitational-wave precursor population.

title: On the Blueprint of Active Galaxies Producing Neutrinos
summary: Based on the observation of the active galaxies NGC 1068 and TXS 0506+056, and on additional evidence for the sources NGC 4151, CGCG 420-015, NGC 7469, and the Circinus Galaxy emerging from IceCube data, we make the case for the production of high-energy neutrinos within a few gravitational radii of supermassive black holes surrounded by a dense plasma radiating X-rays. X-rays represents the target for the production of neutrinos by protons accelerated near the black hole; they also absorb the gamma rays from the decay of neutral pions produced in the same interactions. Neutrinos with energies of tens of TeV and above originate in photoproduction interactions with X-rays of $0.1 \sim 1$\,keV energy on the $Δ$ resonance, $p + γ\rightarrow Δ\rightarrow n + π^+$. Our analysis of the multimessenger data points to gamma-ray-obscured sources with a characteristic neutrino flux linearly proportional to the X-ray flux originating within $\sim 10$ gravitational radii of the black holes, with lower values preferred. We speculate on such sources producing the diffuse flux of neutrinos and cosmic rays of extragalactic origin.

AI.tldr: This paper argues that high-energy neutrinos are produced within a few gravitational radii of supermassive black holes in active galactic nuclei (AGN), based on observations of NGC 1068, TXS 0506+056, and additional IceCube evidence. Neutrinos are produced via photoproduction on X-ray targets (p + γ → Δ → n + π+), with the X-rays also absorbing the accompanying gamma rays. The analysis points to gamma-ray-obscured sources with neutrino flux linearly proportional to X-ray flux from within ~10 gravitational radii, and speculates these sources could produce the diffuse extragalactic neutrino and cosmic-ray fluxes.
AI.motivation: To explain the origin of high-energy neutrinos detected by IceCube from active galaxies, specifically testing whether particle acceleration and neutrino production occur in the immediate vicinity of supermassive black holes surrounded by dense X-ray-emitting plasma.
AI.method: Multimessenger analysis combining IceCube neutrino data with X-ray and gamma-ray observations of several AGN (NGC 1068, TXS 0506+056, NGC 4151, CGCG 420-015, NGC 7469, Circinus Galaxy), examining photoproduction of neutrinos on X-ray targets via the Δ resonance channel.
AI.result: The analysis points to gamma-ray-obscured sources with a characteristic neutrino flux that is linearly proportional to the X-ray flux, originating within ~10 gravitational radii of the black holes, with lower values preferred. These sources could account for the diffuse flux of extragalactic neutrinos and cosmic rays.
AI.conclusion: High-energy neutrinos are produced within a few gravitational radii of supermassive black holes in AGN, where X-rays serve as the target for photoproduction and simultaneously absorb the gamma rays from neutral pion decay. Such gamma-ray-obscured sources may be responsible for the diffuse extragalactic neutrino and cosmic-ray fluxes.

title: Stellar photoionisation modelling in SYNTHESIZER
comment: 29 pages and 29 figures. Submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics
summary: Emission from photoionised gas surrounding young stellar populations ($H\text{II}$ regions) provides critical diagnostics of the physical conditions in star forming galaxies. This emission constrains the gas properties, the nature of ionising sources, and generates essential features for determining galaxy redshifts. To leverage spectroscopic observations to test galaxy formation models, it is essential to incorporate these emissions into synthetic datasets. Here, we present the integration of photoionised gas emission into the SYNTHESIZER package (https://synthesizer-project.github.io) and demonstrate its application. We quantify the impact of key modelling assumptions - including stellar population synthesis models, initial mass functions, ionisation parameter, gas density, geometry, abundance pattern, elemental depletion, and dust - on spectral diagnostics. Furthermore, we demonstrate the versatility of SYNTHESIZER through its application in different scenarios ranging from exploring emission in toy parametric models to large-volume cosmological simulations with realistic star formation and metal enrichment histories. Taken together, SYNTHESIZER provides a flexible, physically motivated framework to model stellar and nebular emissions, serving as a vital link between theory and observations in the era of next-generation spectroscopic missions.

AI.tldr: The paper presents the integration of photoionised gas (H II region) emission into the SYNTHESIZER package, quantifying the impact of key modelling assumptions on spectral diagnostics and demonstrating versatility from toy models to cosmological simulations.
AI.motivation: Emission from photoionised gas surrounding young stellar populations provides critical diagnostics of physical conditions in star-forming galaxies and generates essential features for redshift determination. To test galaxy formation models with next-generation spectroscopic observations, this emission must be incorporated into synthetic datasets.
AI.method: The authors integrate photoionised gas emission into the SYNTHESIZER package (available at synthesizer-project.github.io) and quantify the impact of key modelling assumptions including stellar population synthesis models, IMFs, ionisation parameter, gas density, geometry, abundance pattern, elemental depletion, and dust effects on spectral diagnostics.
AI.result: The paper demonstrates SYNTHESIZER's versatility across applications ranging from toy parametric models to large-volume cosmological simulations with realistic star formation and metal enrichment histories, showing the framework's ability to model both stellar and nebular emissions.
AI.conclusion: SYNTHESIZER provides a flexible, physically motivated framework linking theory and observations, serving as an important tool for the era of next-generation spectroscopic missions.

title: Distinct Jet Properties in the X-Ray-Obscured State of GRS 1915+105
comment: This is a revised manuscript submitted to ApJ
summary: GRS 1915+105 has remained in an X-ray-obscured state since its transition from a long-lasting unobscured state in 2019. We report on 6.7-GHz East Asia VLBI Network observations of GRS 1915+105 obtained during strong radio flares detected at 2.3--11.2 GHz with the RATAN-600 radio telescope in 2025. Our images reveal two contrasting jet morphologies. The first epoch, associated with a flare evolving from an optically thick to an optically thin spectrum, shows a bright radio core accompanied by an extended jet structure. By contrast, the second epoch, observed near the peak of another flare displaying optically thin emission at lower frequencies, is dominated by two bright, symmetric, well-separated jet blobs and shows no detectable radio core. If these jets exhibited the apparent superluminal motions commonly observed prior to 2019, measurable angular shifts would be expected over the five-hour observations. However, no significant jet motion is detected. Combined with our derived jet speed of $βΓ\lesssim 0.40$, these results suggest that the jets launched during the current obscured state are slower than the relativistic jets ($βΓ\gtrsim 1$) observed earlier during the unobscured state. Together with the recently reported large variations in jet orientation, our findings in GRS 1915+105 provide robust support for the emerging paradigm that X-ray binary jets launched in obscured and unobscured states likely exhibit distinct propagation properties.

AI.tldr: This paper reports 6.7-GHz East Asia VLBI Network observations of GRS 1915+105 during radio flares in 2025, while the system remains in an X-ray-obscured state. The observations reveal two contrasting jet morphologies across epochs, and the absence of detectable jet motion combined with a derived jet speed of βΓ≲0.40 suggests that jets in the obscured state are slower than the relativistic jets (βΓ≳1) seen during the earlier unobscured state. This supports the emerging paradigm that X-ray binary jets exhibit distinct propagation properties depending on whether the source is in an obscured or unobscured state.
AI.motivation: To constrain the jet kinematics of GRS 1915+105 during its current X-ray-obscured state, and to test whether jets launched in obscured states have fundamentally slower propagation properties compared to those in unobscured (canonical) states, thereby validating an emerging paradigm in X-ray binary jet studies.
AI.method: The authors used 6.7-GHz East Asia VLBI Network (EAVN) observations of GRS 1915+105 during strong radio flares detected with RATAN-600 (2.3–11.2 GHz), producing high-resolution VLBI images at two epochs. Jet speed was derived from the absence of measurable angular motion over five-hour observations, and compared with historical apparent superluminal measurements from the unobscured state.
AI.result: Two contrasting jet morphologies were imaged: (1) an extended jet structure with a bright core during an optically thick-to-thin evolving flare, and (2) two bright, symmetric, well-separated jet blobs with no detectable core during an optically thin flare peak. No significant jet motion was detected, and the derived jet speed was βΓ≲0.40, well below the relativistic speeds (βΓ≳1) seen pre-2019.
AI.conclusion: The jets launched during the current obscured state of GRS 1915+105 are slower than those observed in the unobscured state. Combined with previously reported large variations in jet orientation, these findings strongly support the emerging paradigm that X-ray binary jets launched in obscured versus unobscured states likely have distinct propagation properties.

title: Galactic HII regions in LAMOST Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic Survey of Nebulae
summary: Based on LAMOST Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic Survey of Nebulae (MRS-N) data and WISE Galactic HII region catalog, we construct a sample of 280 Galactic HII regions and candidates in the Outer Galaxy (80$^{\circ}$ $\lesssim$ l $\lesssim$ 220$^{\circ}$). Using MRS-N optical spectra, we measure four emission lines (H$α$, [NII]$λ$6584, [SII]$λλ$6717,6731) and use line-ratios to spectroscopically confirm 255 HII regions, including 90 previously "Known" HII regions and 165 newly classified ones. We measure their $T_{\rm e}$, $n_{\rm e}$ and oxygen abundance, and determine distances via associated OB stars and the kinematic method. The sample spans $R_{\rm gal}$ from 8.16 to 15.36 kpc, enabling investigation of radial gradients in physical properties. We find [NII]/H$α$ and [SII]/H$α$ decrease with increasing $R_{\rm gal}$, while [SII]/[NII] remains nearly flat; these trends are quite different from diffuse ionized gas (DIG). We derive the $T_{\rm e}$ gradient of 344.530 $\pm$ 78.083 K kpc$^{-1}$, and the $\log n_{\rm e}$ gradient of -0.143 $\pm$ 0.041 cm$^{-3}$ kpc$^{-1}$. Oxygen abundance shows a steep slope of -0.044 $\pm$ 0.010 dex kpc$^{-1}$ in the inner disk and a shallow slope of -0.016 $\pm$ 0.005 dex kpc$^{-1}$ in the outer disk, with a global slope of -0.014 $\pm$ 0.005 dex kpc$^{-1}$. We also examine the two-dimensional distributions of $T_{\rm e}$, $n_{\rm e}$, and oxygen abundance, and find the gradients vary with azimuth. There is no obvious difference between spiral arm and interarm regions, and no trend appears along individual arms. From [NII]/H$α$-[SII]$λ$6717/H$α$ diagram, HII regions have a S$^+$/S ratio (0.32), lower than DIG (0.43); however, heavy overlap prevents clear separation from this diagram alone.

AI.tldr: Based on LAMOST MRS-N data and WISE HII region catalog, 280 Galactic HII regions/candidates in the Outer Galaxy (80°≤l≤220°) are constructed. Spectroscopic confirmation of 255 HII regions yields measurements of electron temperature, density, and oxygen abundance, revealing radial gradients, azimuthal variations, and differences from diffuse ionized gas.
AI.motivation: To investigate the physical properties and radial gradients of HII regions in the Outer Galaxy, which is less studied than the inner Galaxy, using a large spectroscopic sample from LAMOST MRS-N.
AI.method: Construct a sample of 280 HII regions from LAMOST MRS-N and WISE catalog; measure Hα, [NII]λ6584, [SII]λλ6717,6731 emission lines; use line-ratios for spectroscopic confirmation; measure T_e, n_e, oxygen abundance; determine distances via OB stars and kinematic method.
AI.result: 255 HII regions confirmed (90 known, 165 new). Found [NII]/Hα and [SII]/Hα decrease with R_gal while [SII]/[NII] stays flat. T_e gradient of 344.530±78.083 K kpc⁻¹, log n_e gradient of -0.143±0.041 cm⁻³ kpc⁻¹, oxygen abundance slope of -0.044±0.010 dex kpc⁻¹ (inner) and -0.016±0.005 dex kpc⁻¹ (outer), global -0.014±0.005 dex kpc⁻¹. Gradients vary azimuthally; no spiral arm vs interarm differences.
AI.conclusion: HII regions in the Outer Galaxy exhibit distinct radial gradients and azimuthal variations in physical properties, differing from diffuse ionized gas. Oxygen abundance gradient steepens in the inner disk and flattens outward, while [NII]/Hα-[SII]/Hα diagrams show heavy overlap between HII regions and DIG, limiting their separation.

title: eRASSU J043115.8-711730: The first pulsating symbiotic super-soft X-ray source in the Magellanic Bridge
summary: The Magellanic Bridge stellar population is a relic of the tidal interaction between the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds. A comprehensive view of the evolution of the Bridge stellar population requires probing the compact remnants of stellar evolution, otherwise hidden at optical wavelengths. The all-sky survey conducted by the eROSITA instrument on-board the Spectrum Roentgen Gamma observatory has discovered a significant population of compact-object-powered systems in the Bridge using X-ray. The candidate super-soft source eRASSU J043115.8-711730 (hereafter J0431-71) was discovered as a part of this campaign, and we present here a deeper study of this source using XMM-Newton and SALT spectroscopy, long-term optical-infrared photometry using OGLE, ATLAS, ASAS-SN, WISE, and GAIA data. J0431-71 is a highly variable super-soft X-ray source, classified as a red giant with the GAIA color-magnitude diagram. The source exhibits: (a) a thermal X-ray spectrum with a temperature of kT$\sim$30 eV and a bright state luminosity of $3.2\times10^37$~erg~s$^{-1}$ in the 0.15-1 keV band, (b) Balmer emission lines, [Fe X] coronal line, HeII emission, and the Bowen fluorescence blend, (c) an optical and infrared periodicity of $\sim$500-560 days in phase with the X-ray-UV emission, (d) a 'redder-when-brighter' trend in the stellar emission with a $\sim$520 day period indicating a pulsating donor star. We argue that the observed spectral and temporal properties in J0431-71 are consistent with a high-accretion rate onto a white-dwarf via Roche-lobe overflow, making J0431-71 the first symbiotic source discovered in the Bridge.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a deep multi-wavelength study of the super-soft X-ray source eRASSU J043115.8-711730 (J0431-71) in the Magellanic Bridge, discovered by eROSITA. Using XMM-Newton, SALT, OGLE, ATLAS, ASAS-SN, WISE, and GAIA data, the authors characterize it as a highly variable super-soft source with a ~30 eV thermal X-ray spectrum, optical/IR periodicity of ~500-560 days, and a redder-when-brighter trend. They conclude J0431-71 is a symbiotic system (white dwarf accreting via Roche-lobe overflow from a pulsating red giant donor), making it the first such source discovered in the Bridge.
AI.motivation: To probe the compact remnants of stellar evolution in the Magellanic Bridge—a tidal debris region between the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds—by studying X-ray-discovered compact-object-powered systems, thereby completing the picture of the Bridge's stellar population that is hidden at optical wavelengths.
AI.method: Multi-wavelength follow-up observations using XMM-Newton (X-ray spectroscopy), SALT (optical spectroscopy), and long-term optical-infrared photometry from OGLE, ATLAS, ASAS-SN, WISE, and GAIA. The authors analyze the X-ray spectrum, optical emission lines, photometric periodicity, and color-magnitude variations.
AI.result: J0431-71 exhibits a thermal X-ray spectrum (kT~30 eV, L~3.2×10^37 erg/s in 0.15-1 keV), Balmer/[Fe X]/HeII/Bowen fluorescence emission lines, ~500-560 day optical-IR periodicity in phase with X-ray-UV emission, and a redder-when-brighter trend with ~520 day period indicating a pulsating donor star.
AI.conclusion: The spectral and temporal properties of J0431-71 are consistent with high-accretion-rate Roche-lobe overflow onto a white dwarf from a pulsating red-giant donor, identifying it as a symbiotic system—the first such source found in the Magellanic Bridge.

title: The X-ray-Weak Tail of the Quasar Population: Physical Properties and Redshift Evolution of Variability-Selected AGN in eFEDS
summary: (abridged) Aims: To characterize variability-selected AGN candidates within the eROSITA Final Equatorial-Depth Survey (eFEDS), leveraging the synergy between optical variability and deep X-ray observations by SRG (Spectrum Roentgen Gamma)/eROSITA, to compare the physical properties of AGN populations selected through complementary methods. Methods: We used a sample of AGN candidates selected via optical variability by Arévalo et al. and cross-match it to the X-ray selected eFEDS AGN sample. Spectroscopic characterizations are obtained for the matched samples from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument public data products. Results: We find a high classification purity with 98% candidates confirmed as broad-line AGN/QSOs. We identify a significant population (25%) that lack X-ray counterparts (X-U) in the eFEDS survey. We find that the X-D and X-U samples exhibit distinct physical properties and redshift distributions. The X-U sample peaks at $z = 2$ while the X-D sample at $z =1$, with nearly half of the variability-selected AGN at $z > 2.5$ remaining undetected in X-rays. This missing fraction can be attributed to K-correction effects and SED evolution with luminosity, mainly resulting in high accretion rate objects falling out of the X-D sample at higher redshifts. X-ray variability accounts for a part of the missing fraction but its dependence with redshift is less clear. Ensemble spectral analysis reveals that X-D sources have steeper optical continua and stronger broad emission lines than their X-U counterparts, while the forbidden and semi-forbidden lines have equal EWs in both samples. Finally, broad absorption line (BAL) features are found almost exclusively in the X-U population. This "missing" X-ray population must be accounted for when extrapolating X-ray-selected AGN to the broader Type I population and could impact cosmic estimates of massive black hole growth.

AI.tldr: This paper characterizes variability-selected AGN candidates from the eFEDS survey using eROSITA X-ray data and DESI spectroscopy. Of the optical-variability-selected AGN, 98% are confirmed broad-line AGN/QSOs, but 25% lack X-ray counterparts. The X-ray-undetected (X-U) population peaks at z=2 (vs z=1 for X-ray-detected sources), and nearly half of variability-selected AGN at z>2.5 remain X-ray invisible due to K-correction, SED evolution, and partial X-ray variability effects. X-U sources show flatter optical continua, weaker broad emission lines, and almost exclusively host BAL features.
AI.motivation: To characterize variability-selected AGN candidates within eFEDS by leveraging the synergy between optical variability and deep X-ray observations from SRG/eROSITA, and to compare the physical properties of AGN populations selected through complementary (optical variability vs. X-ray) methods.
AI.method: Cross-matched a sample of optically variability-selected AGN candidates (from Arévalo et al.) against the X-ray-selected eFEDS AGN sample, with spectroscopic characterization from DESI public data products, including ensemble spectral analysis and redshift distribution comparisons.
AI.result: 98% of variability-selected candidates are confirmed as broad-line AGN/QSOs. 25% lack X-ray counterparts (X-U). X-U sources peak at z=2 while X-ray-detected (X-D) sources peak at z=1; ~50% of variability-selected AGN at z>2.5 are X-ray undetected. The missing fraction stems largely from K-correction and luminosity-dependent SED evolution, with X-ray variability contributing marginally. X-D sources have steeper optical continua and stronger broad lines; BAL features are almost exclusively found in the X-U population.
AI.conclusion: The X-ray "missing" AGN population must be accounted for when extrapolating X-ray-selected AGN samples to the broader Type I population, as their omission could bias cosmic estimates of massive black hole growth.

title: Comprehensive X-ray Study of Giant Radio Galaxies with XMM-Newton and Chandra
comment: Accepted for publication in JHEAp , 21 pages, 7 figures, 12 tables
summary: We present a systematic X-ray spectral analysis of 27 giant radio galaxies (GRGs) using archival \textit{XMM-Newton} and \textit{Chandra} data. Roughly 44\% of the sample show intrinsic absorption ($N_{\mathrm{H,int}} \gtrsim 10^{21}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$), while several exhibit narrow Fe K$α$ emission lines with equivalent widths up to $\sim$570 eV. Soft X-ray features are also common, including thermal plasma emission (kT$\sim 0.2$--0.8 keV) and ionized absorbers, in some cases consistent with high-velocity outflows. The photon indices are typically hard (median $ Γ\sim 1.6$), in line with radio-loud AGN. A comparison between nuclear X-ray luminosity and extended radio power shows that many sources host relatively strong X-ray cores compared to their lobes, pointing toward possible restarted nuclear activity. For 10 GRGs with published black hole masses, we explore preliminary relations with X-ray luminosity, Eddington ratio, and photon index. We find a positive trend between $M_{\rm BH}$ and $L_{2-10\,{\rm keV}}$, while Eddington ratios show no clear dependence on mass. A tentative negative relation between $λ_{\rm Edd}$ and $Γ$ hints at inefficient accretion, although confirmation will require larger samples. Overall, GRGs display diverse nuclear conditions and accretion states, supporting scenarios where obscuration, episodic or restarted activity, and low-efficiency accretion shape their long-term evolution.

AI.tldr: A systematic X-ray spectral analysis of 27 giant radio galaxies using archival XMM-Newton and Chandra data, revealing diverse nuclear conditions including intrinsic absorption, Fe Kα emission lines, thermal plasma, ionized outflows, and a tentative negative Eddington ratio–photon index trend suggesting inefficient accretion.
AI.motivation: Giant radio galaxies represent the largest known radio structures in the universe, yet their nuclear X-ray properties and accretion states are poorly characterized. This work aims to systematically probe their central engine conditions, including absorption, emission lines, outflows, and accretion energetics.
