AI.result: The PRF yields higher stability and robustness for ambiguous candidates than XGBoost, while the two classifiers occupy complementary regimes: XGBoost achieves higher recall in balanced/high-precision scenarios with rigid decision boundaries, whereas PRF rejects more false positives by penalizing sources with large feature uncertainties. Applying the framework to archival data identified 11 new candidate TDEs from unclassified populations and 3 potential photometric TDEs previously misclassified as SNe or AGNs.
AI.conclusion: TDEs can be reliably identified using photometric lightcurve features alone, providing a host-independent framework. Uncertainty-aware probabilistic classifiers are essential for the Rubin era to prevent the overconfident misclassifications inherent in deterministic models at low signal-to-noise ratios.

title: Same explosion, many faces: numerical modeling reveals viewing angle as a driver of diversity for core-collapse SNe in binary systems
comment: 19 pages, 12 figures, submitted to AAS journals. Comments are welcome
summary: Observable properties of core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) depend sensitively on the circumstellar material (CSM) formed by pre-explosion mass loss from the progenitor star. Since a large fraction of CCSN progenitors reside in binaries, both the progenitor structure and surrounding CSM can be significantly impacted by binary interaction. Yet, its impact on the observed CCSN landscape remains poorly constrained. In this work, we investigate CCSNe from binary systems undergoing stable Roche lobe overflow. We construct a suite of binary evolution models in \texttt{MESA} with a fixed initial primary mass ($16M_{\odot}$), exploring secondary masses in the range $12-15M_{\odot}$ and initial orbital periods $>500$ days. We generate three-dimensional (3D) CSM structures from the resulting mass-loss histories and orbital dynamics, extract angle-dependent density profiles along three lines of sight, and compute multi-band light curves with the radiation-hydrodynamics code \texttt{Stella}. We find that binary-driven CSM develops highly aspherical morphologies, governed by the orbital period and the mass ratio. Interaction between SN ejecta and this structured medium produces pronounced viewing-angle dependence in the light curves, with peak luminosities differing by factors of $\sim5$ and late-time $B-V$ colors varying by $\sim1.5$ mag depending on observer orientation. We further show that interpreting such events with one-dimensional frameworks assuming isolated progenitors and spherical winds can introduce biases up to $50\%$ for inferred explosion properties and $>200\%$ for inferred mass-loss rates. Our results are consistent with a substantial fraction of interacting Type II SN diversity arising from binary-shaped asymmetric CSM and viewing-angle effects, motivating multidimensional approaches to interpreting these transients.

However, the impact of binary interaction on the observed CCSN landscape remains poorly constrained. Understanding how binary-driven CSM shapes observed supernova properties is crucial for interpreting these transients correctly.

title: Search for gravitational waves associated with high-energy neutrinos detected by IceCube during the third observing run of LIGO-Virgo
summary: We search for generic gravitational-wave transients associated with high-energy neutrinos detected by the IceCube Neutrino Observatory during the third Observing Run (O3) of Advanced LIGO, Advanced Virgo, and KAGRA. We perform an unmodeled, targeted search, which is sensitive to gravitational-wave signals weaker than those reported in real time or in the gravitional-wave transient catalog, and can thus uncover coincidences missed by typical neutrino follow-up searches. We find no statistically significant gravitational-wave signal and set lower bounds on the distance of possible gravitational-wave sources for different emission models.

AI.tldr: We perform an unmodeled, targeted search for gravitational-wave transients coincident with IceCube high-energy neutrinos during LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA's third Observing Run (O3), finding no significant signal and setting lower-bound distance limits for various emission models.
AI.motivation: To uncover gravitational-wave-neutrino coincidences that may have been missed by typical real-time or catalog-based follow-up searches, by exploiting an unmodeled search sensitive to weaker gravitational-wave signals.
AI.method: An unmodeled, targeted search for generic gravitational-wave transients associated with high-energy neutrinos detected by IceCube during O3.
AI.result: No statistically significant gravitational-wave signal was found; lower bounds on source distances were set for different emission models.
AI.conclusion: The absence of significant coincident gravitational-wave signals constrains the distance (and hence luminosity) of possible gravitational-wave-emitting neutrino sources during O3.

title: Spinning down neutron-star merger remnants with the Tayler-Spruit dynamo: Global simulations reveal the formation of massive disks and neutron-rich ejecta
summary: Magnetic-field amplification and angular momentum (AM) transport critically shape the secular evolution, lifetime, and electromagnetic signatures of binary neutron-star merger remnants. While the magnetorotational instability can operate in the outer negative-shear regions of the neutron-star remnant and accretion disk, the positive-shear, stably stratified core may instead be susceptible to the Tayler-Spruit dynamo. We present the first global, long-term general-relativistic neutrino-radiation magnetohydrodynamics simulations of a neutron-star merger remnant incorporating the unresolved Tayler-Spruit dynamo through a new mean-field dynamo subgrid prescription. Our axisymmetric simulations starting from a realistic merger remnant show that the Tayler-Spruit dynamo is primarily active in high-latitude regions of the remnant core. The resulting Maxwell stresses redistribute AM on a spin-down timescale of a few hundred milliseconds, substantially flattening the core rotation profile and transferring mass and AM from the outer remnant into the disk. This produces a more massive, extended, and strongly magnetized disk with a low electron fraction, leading to substantially more neutron-rich ejecta. Our results demonstrate that currently unmodelled Tayler-Spruit dynamo action can qualitatively alter the rotational evolution, collapse prospects, disk formation, and multi-messenger signatures of long-lived neutron-star merger remnants.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first global, long-term general-relativistic neutrino-radiation magnetohydrodynamics simulations of a neutron-star merger remnant incorporating the unresolved Tayler-Spruit dynamo via a new mean-field subgrid prescription. The dynamo, active mainly in high-latitude regions of the remnant core, produces Maxwell stresses that redistribute angular momentum on a few hundred-millisecond timescale, flattening the core's rotation profile and transferring mass/AM into the disk, resulting in a more massive, extended, strongly magnetized, low electron-fraction disk with more neutron-rich ejecta. This demonstrates that unmodelled Tayler-Spruit dynamo action can qualitatively alter rotational evolution, collapse prospects, disk formation, and multi-messenger signatures of long-lived merger remnants.
AI.motivation: To understand how magnetic-field amplification and angular momentum transport shape the secular evolution, lifetime, and electromagnetic signatures of binary neutron-star merger remnants, specifically addressing the unexplored role of the Tayler-Spruit dynamo in the positive-shear, stably stratified remnant core, where the magnetorotational instability is ineffective.
AI.method: Global, long-term general-relativistic neutrino-radiation magnetohydrodynamics (GRMHD) simulations of a neutron-star merger remnant, incorporating the unresolved Tayler-Spruit dynamo through a new mean-field dynamo subgrid prescription. The simulations are axisymmetric and start from a realistic merger remnant.
AI.result: The Tayler-Spruit dynamo is primarily active in high-latitude regions of the remnant core. Maxwell stresses redistribute angular momentum on a spin-down timescale of a few hundred milliseconds, substantially flattening the core rotation profile and transferring mass and angular momentum from the outer remnant into the disk. This yields a more massive, extended, and strongly magnetized disk with low electron fraction, producing substantially more neutron-rich ejecta.
AI.conclusion: Currently unmodelled Tayler-Spruit dynamo action can qualitatively alter the rotational evolution, collapse prospects, disk formation, and multi-messenger signatures of long-lived neutron-star merger remnants, underscoring the need to include this mechanism for accurate astrophysical modeling.

title: A Four-dimensional Model-agnostic Probe into the Astrophysical Origins of Binary Black Hole Subpopulations
summary: There is strong evidence of multiple binary black hole~(BBH) subpopulations in the cumulative gravitational wave catalog by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration that likely originate through distinct evolutionary channels. The astrophysical interpretation of this complex underlying population is subject to theoretical uncertainties in treatments of binary stellar evolution, core collapse, and host environments. Due to a lack of robust predictions and the sheer diversity of plausible features, strongly modelled population analyses often lead to prior-driven conclusions. On the other hand, flexible alternatives are often difficult to scale in higher dimensions, which can lead to a loss of critical information on astrophysically meaningful correlations. In this \textit{Letter}, we present the first data-driven reconstruction of the joint four-dimensional distribution of BBH primary masses, mass ratios, effective inspiral and effective precessing spin parameters, which yields novel model-agnostic constraints on the astrophysical origins of BBH subpopulations. We characterize four distinct subpopulations spanning different ranges of BBH masses and report new correlations in these specific mass ranges that are beyond the reach of strongly modeled parametrizations and lower-dimensional data-driven frameworks. Our results unveil novel insights into the abundances of specific subchannels of isolated binary evolution, dynamical assembly, and hierarchical mergers across various mass ranges in the astrophysical BBH population.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first data-driven reconstruction of the joint four-dimensional distribution of binary black hole (BBH) primary masses, mass ratios, effective inspiral, and effective precessing spin parameters from the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA catalog, identifying four distinct subpopulations and revealing new astrophysically meaningful correlations in specific mass ranges.
AI.motivation: Strongly modelled population analyses of BBH subpopulations are often prior-driven due to theoretical uncertainties in binary stellar evolution, core collapse, and host environments. Flexible alternatives struggle to scale in higher dimensions, losing critical information on astrophysically meaningful correlations. A model-agnostic, high-dimensional approach is needed.
AI.method: The authors perform a data-driven reconstruction of the joint four-dimensional distribution of BBH primary masses, mass ratios, effective inspiral spin, and effective precessing spin parameters, using a flexible framework that scales to higher dimensions to extract model-agnostic constraints on subpopulations.
AI.result: Four distinct BBH subpopulations are characterized across different mass ranges, with new correlations reported that are beyond the reach of strongly modeled parametrizations and lower-dimensional data-driven frameworks. Novel insights into the abundances of isolated binary evolution, dynamical assembly, and hierarchical merger subchannels are unveiled.
AI.conclusion: The model-agnostic four-dimensional reconstruction provides new astrophysical constraints on the origins of BBH subpopulations, offering insights into specific evolutionary channels (isolated binary evolution, dynamical assembly, hierarchical mergers) that were previously inaccessible with existing methods.
